authority.policy: No legal rule was added or inferred from prose.
authority.routeConsumers: MD pardon_signed_date mirrors ROUTE_ESCALATION_FACT_IDS; MD arrest_date mirrors an existing legal-authority screeningFactId. Missouri carries two: mo_at_least_twenty_two is the approximate screening threshold and appears in the § 311.326 screeningFactIds; date_of_birth is the exact clock and appears only in that contract's packetReleasePreconditions, so it is collected after the claim and never in free screening.
authority.exactPacketFactIds: Existing structural/date questions plus Mississippi's unsupported projection-added exact dates and dependent fine-imposed fact. MD pardon_signed_date, MD arrest_date, and MO date_of_birth are exact packet/final-verification facts on only their approved routeConsumers pathways. MO mo_at_least_twenty_two is deliberately absent: it is an approximate threshold, not an exact date, and treating it as a packet fact would put it behind the claim where screening needs it.
authority.freeTimingBoundary: The generic resolved_timing_bucket describes time since case resolution, so it is not reused for Maryland's arrest/pardon deadlines or Missouri's age-21 clock. Those routes remain fail-closed without protected exact authority; each owning packet plan retains its exact fact and the free selector never renders it.
authority.completionAliasIds: Existing completion aliases only where the projected profile also carries the canonical court_requirements_completed authority fact.

blockers: No approved pathway mapping exists for the five Mississippi ms_* date facts or ms_mip_fine_imposed; they remain packet-only and no predicate was invented.
Lane B metadata validation must admit approved projection-added question IDs used by MD, MS, and MO lifecycle metadata.
